name: the-claude-factory
description: Production-grade Claude Code plugins that automate and optimize everyday workflows: skills, agents, hooks, MCP and LSP servers, and more.

plugins.name: bash-lsp-intelligence
plugins.description: Gives Claude Code bash-language-server for Bash and POSIX shell scripts, plus a skill that teaches Claude to trace sourced files and same-named functions, fix ShellCheck and shfmt findings without changing behavior, and verify every change with evidence.

plugins.name: plugin-test-bench
plugins.description: Proves your Claude Code plugin works the way your users receive it: installs a copy in a throwaway config, checks it loads, runs your eval suite against that copy, and reviews your eval cases so they measure what the plugin adds.

plugins.name: python-lsp-intelligence
plugins.description: Gives Claude Code the basedpyright language server for Python, plus a skill that teaches Claude to resolve symbols, aliases and imports semantically, fix basedpyright and Ruff findings without suppressing them, and verify every change with evidence.

plugins.name: session-handoff
plugins.description: Carries a project's working state from one session to the next: write a handoff when you stop, and the next session reads it, reports what is still open and asks you where to start.

plugins.name: skill-diagnostics
plugins.description: Audits Claude skills for best-practice conformance, portability and whether a model can run them without guessing, with file-and-line evidence and one verdict.

plugins.name: typescript6-lsp-intelligence
plugins.description: Gives Claude Code a pinned TypeScript 6 language server for TypeScript and JavaScript, checks every file Claude edits with the matching compiler, and teaches Claude to navigate by symbol and fix compiler findings without unsafe assertions or suppressions.

plugins.name: typescript7-lsp-intelligence
plugins.description: Gives Claude Code the native TypeScript 7 language server for TypeScript and JavaScript, plus a skill that teaches Claude to check which program owns a file, fix compiler findings without unsafe assertions or suppressions, and verify every change with evidence.
